instantiated_cells.cited_section: Wis. Stat. § 13.68 (2025) (Principal’s expense statement); § 13.68(4) (reports by lobbyist to principal)
instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires principals (not lobbyists) to file periodic expense statements, while lobbyists only provide information to principals for inclusion in the principal’s statement.
The only periodic filing cadence specified for expense statements is twice yearly (July 31 and January 31), not annually.
Expense statements are due on or before July 31 and January 31, so monthly lobbyist spending reports are not required.
The statute sets semiannual deadlines for expense statements and does not provide for quarterly lobbyist spending reports.
Although principals file semiannual expense statements, the statute does not require lobbyists to file their own periodic spending reports.
No triannual cadence is specified; the statute provides only January 31 and July 31 deadlines for principal expense statements.
The statute specifies a single semiannual filing schedule for principal expense statements and does not create any other lobbyist spending report cadence.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Wis. Stat. § 13.68(1) (principal’s statement required); § 13.68(4) (lobbyist provides info to principal)
instantiated_cells.justification: The law requires principals to report aggregate lobbying expenditures, but does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report to include total expenditures.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Wis. Stat. § 13.68(1)(a)1. (compensation to lobbyists reported by principal)
instantiated_cells.justification: Compensation to lobbyists must be included in the principal’s aggregate total, but no separate lobbyist spending report is required to disclose total compensation.
The principal’s statement lists amounts paid to each lobbyist (by principal), but the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed report breaking compensation down by payer.
The required expense statement is filed by principals and calls for aggregate totals and certain listings, not a lobbyist-filed itemized spending report.
Because the statute does not require a lobbyist to file a periodic spending report, it does not mandate that such a lobbyist report use an itemized format.
The statute’s reporting requirements apply to principals and do not require a lobbyist periodic spending report that categorizes expenses by type.
Office overhead and related indirect costs are reported by the principal when applicable, but no lobbyist-filed spending report is required to include indirect costs.
Topic/issue identification duties are imposed on principals, not via a lobbyist periodic spending report.
The statute requires principals to report topics with reasonable specificity, but it does not require a lobbyist periodic spending report to include general subject matter.
Legislative proposal/proposed rule identifiers are reported by principals under § 13.67(1), not in any required lobbyist spending report.
The principal must report each legislative proposal and proposed administrative rule number, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report including bill numbers.
The statute requires identification of proposals/topics but does not require any lobbyist spending report (or principal report) to state a position for/against a bill.
Principals must keep a daily time record (including meeting time) but the statute does not require a lobbyist spending report listing contacts made.
The statute requires time proportion estimates by topic for principals meeting a 10% threshold, not expenditure-per-issue reporting in a lobbyist spending report.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Wis. Stat. § 13.625(1g) (generally prohibits furnishing); § 13.68(1)(d) (reimbursement under § 13.621(7)(a) reported by principal)
instantiated_cells.justification: The statute largely prohibits such items and requires principals to report certain reimbursements, but does not require a lobbyist periodic spending report to disclose gifts/entertainment/transport/lodging.
The required periodic filing is a principal expense statement and does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report containing the lobbyist’s contact information.
The statute requires principal-filed expense statements and does not impose any lobbyist spending report requirement to list principal names.
No lobbyist periodic spending report is required, so the statute does not require such a report to include principal contact information.
Business nature/purpose information is required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist periodic spending report.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Wis. Stat. § 13.68(1) (every registered principal must file)
instantiated_cells.justification: Because the statute does not require lobbyists to file periodic spending reports at all, it likewise does not impose a lobbyist 'no activity' report requirement.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Wis. Stat. § 13.68(1)(d) (reimbursements to specified officials/candidates only); § 13.625(4m)(d) (relatives/household of lobbyist/principal)
instantiated_cells.justification: Reporting in § 13.68(1)(d) concerns reimbursements to specified officials/candidates and does not extend to household members of officials in any lobbyist spending report.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because no lobbyist periodic spending report is required and no alternative cadence is defined, there is no 'other' cadence to specify.
